documents.title: Basis and Use of this Logbook
documents.description: Purpose of the logbook, rating scale and resident responsibilities.

sections.heading: Basis and use
paragraphs: This logbook is based on the NMC revised competency-based postgraduate MD Paediatrics curriculum. The curriculum describes outcome-based competencies across newborn-to-adolescent care, ambulatory and inpatient care, healthy/ill child care, prevention, family-centred care, emergency care and intensive care.

NMC guidance requires real-time documentation of postings, work done in wards/OPDs/casualty and other areas, procedures assisted/performed and teaching sessions; the logbook is used for periodic faculty assessment, feedback and internal evaluation.
Suggested case/procedure numbers are training targets and should be adapted to the current university/NMC requirements, institutional workload and available facilities.

sections.heading: Resident responsibilities
bullets: Maintain confidentiality; do not enter patient names.
Bring logbook for monthly and quarterly reviews.
Complete required research, teaching and academic activities.

documents.title: Three-Year Rotation Plan
documents.description: Year-wise rotation framework and the suggested monthly distribution of key activities (Appendix).

notes: *Suggested institutional framework; modify to local university/NMC-approved rotation schedule.

monthlyPriorities.priority: Orientation, history/examination, ward/OPD, newborn examination, anthropometry, basic procedures
Neonatology/SNCU, emergency, resuscitation, nutrition, common infections
Advanced ward/NICU/PICU, subspecialty exposure, research/data collection
Critical care, procedures, advanced case management, teaching
Research completion, audit, advanced competencies, exam preparation
Final consolidation, competency sign-off, dissertation and exit assessment

documents.title: Competency Master Index
documents.description: The 22 institutional competencies used across logs, assessments and final sign-off.

notes: Important: competency codes are organized as an institutional mapping/index rather than reproducing the copyrighted curriculum verbatim. The department should cross-check the latest NMC curriculum and university regulations before final adoption.
Expected progression for every competency is PS ? PI.

documents.title: Suggested Minimum Clinical Exposure Targets
documents.description: Suggested cumulative exposure targets over the three-year programme.

distribution: Mini-CEX and DOPS: about six of each per year (18 each over three years).
Journal clubs and seminars: about six of each per year.
Case-based discussions: about one per month (36 over three years).
Clinical audits / M&M: about two per year.
UG teaching sessions: about four per year.
Admissions, OPD and emergency encounters accumulate across postings in proportion to the rotation plan.
guidance: Record every encounter in the appropriate log on the day it occurs, using anonymised case references only.
Submit entries for faculty verification promptly; officially reviewed progress counts faculty-verified entries only.
Link each entry to the relevant competency codes where applicable so that competency progression can be reviewed.
Progress figures in the app are calculated automatically from your stored records; they cannot be entered manually.
notes: These are suggested departmental training targets, not claimed NMC-mandated numbers. Adjust to patient volume, simulation availability, university rules and documented competence.

documents.title: Suggested Procedure Targets
documents.description: Suggested cumulative procedure and skill targets over the three-year programme.

distribution: Progress from observing (O) and assisting (A) in PGY-1 towards supervised (PS) and independent (PI) performance by PGY-3.
guidance: Log every procedure with your role (O/A/PS/PI), any complication and your reflection.
Each procedure log entry counts once towards the matching procedure target.
Use DOPS for formal direct observation of key procedures.
notes: These are suggested departmental training targets, not claimed NMC-mandated numbers. Adjust to patient volume, simulation availability, university rules and documented competence.
